persona.role: local resident and former bar worker

sent_to_model:
I need help writing an online review of a new bar and restaurant in my neighborhood. My wife and I went in hoping we'd finally have another local place worth going to, but I left pretty annoyed about what we got for the money. I've lived around here a few years and have worked in a bar myself, so I have something to compare it with. I'd like a fairly detailed review covering the atmosphere and drinks, our two dinners, and why I think the prices are out of line for this area. The waiter made a big deal about everything being freshly made, which I didn't believe after eating it. I want other locals to know why I won't be returning under the current management.

- Both dinners cost $14 each.
- Previously worked in a bar offering 700 different beers.
- The premises used to be a Timbers.
- Wife ordered Linguini Alfredo; garlic bread included.
- Spirits list included Dom priced at $400.
- Lived in this neighborhood for several years.
- Burger included sweet potato fries, bacon and fried pickle chips.
- Video Poker machines in bar; liquor selection behind bar appeared limited.
- Smiths Ale stood out among the beers.
- Pasta protein and vegetable additions cost extra; chicken, fish and shrimp weren't available.
- Drinks menu separated canned beers into their own category.
- Interior so poorly lit that obstacles seemed easy to stumble over.
- Waiter said everything was prepared fresh; seemed very inexperienced at serving.
- Burger patty possibly shaped by hand, estimated weight one-third pound.
- Sweet potato fries insufficiently cooked; pickle chips became soft sitting on burger.
- Bacon tasted as though previously cooked and briefly put through the fryer.
- Wife's meal was pasta, sauce and bread without any included meat or vegetables.
- Food seemed like Sysco prepared products heated for service; fresh preparation claim wasn't believable.
- Alfredo tasted poor; pasta didn't seem fresh and bread seemed bought in. No bolognaise noticed among red sauce choices.
- North Western decor left over from Timbers felt predictable; bar atmosphere uncomfortable and unremarkable.
- Wine selection unusual and expensive; overall beer range unimpressive. Separate cans category odd given familiar canned British Cream Ales.
- Prices unsuitable for neighborhood; food quality and portions didn't justify cost. Doubt business will last; expensive bottles unlikely to sell.
- Wanted an affordable neighborhood bar and restaurant; visit failed to meet that hope.
- Warn prospective customers about poor value; won't revisit unless management changes.

(About me: local resident and former bar worker, United States. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Describe the atmosphere and assess the drinks selection.
Describe both dinners and why their quality made the fresh preparation claim unconvincing.
Explain why the prices represent poor value for the neighborhood.
State that a return visit would require a change in management.
